PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to the regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk’s Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us. Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City's system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

minutes_text:
MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  July 13, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:07 p.m. on July
13, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
Mayor Khan announced that City Hall was now open to the public, allowing members of
the public to physically attend and participate in City Council meetings, and noted the
current guidelines for face coverings. She also noted that 1) the meeting was broadcast
live on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99,
and livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org; 2) members of the public would continue to
have the ability to provide live comments on agenda items via Zoom; and 3) the City of
Irvine continued to sanitize surfaces and equipment in the Council Chamber and
throughout City Hall.

In addition, Carl Petersen, City Clerk, provided instructions on how to participate in the
meeting; and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended, which allowed
members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on all agenda items, which
would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the City’s website.
 City Council Minutes  July 13, 2021

  Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
  not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Mayor Kim led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Paul Han from Mariners Church provided the invocation.

  1.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  1.1  Orange County Mosquito and Vector Control District

  This item was agendized at the request of Vice Mayor Kim as the City’s
  representative to the Orange County Mosquito and Vector Control
  District (OCMVCD), who requested a presentation related to the
  various resources and services that OCMVCD could provide to Irvine
  residents.

  Richard Howard, District Manager, OCMVCD, provided a brief overview
  of OCMVCD’s role and the services it provides.

  City Council discussion included: clarifying when a resident should call
  for an exterminator versus the OCMVCD; questioned the differences
  between fire and regular ants, as well as rats and mice; inquired about
  the largest contributors for mosquitoes in Irvine; inquired about the
  average cost for OCMVCD services to property owners annually;
  questioned whether a change in types of vectors have been realized
  due to climate change; inquired about OCMVCD’s outreach to
  Homeowner Associations (HOAs) regarding community pools;
  suggested that the staff provide a master list of Irvine HOAs to
  OCMVCD; and recommended that a town hall be held for residents
  highlighting the services offered by OCMVCD.

  Received and filed.

  1.2  Irvine Police Department Diversity Recruitment Efforts

  This item was agendized at the request of Vice Mayor Kim and
  Councilmember Kuo, who requested a presentation on the Irvine Police
  Department’s efforts to recruit personnel that would better reflect the
  diverse makeup of the City.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  July 13, 2021

  Mike Hamel, Chief of Police/Director of Public Safety, and James Do,
  Police Sergeant, provided a brief presentation and responded to
  questions.

  City Council discussion included: reiterating the City’s efforts to
  promote diversity, equity, and inclusion; clarified the meaning of
  diversity recruitment; questioned whether ethnic media was being
  leveraged for recruitment purposes; inquired about recruitment efforts
  within Irvine colleges and universities; questioned whether a contracted
  police academy existed, and whether the curriculum reflected Irvine’s
  values; noted receipt of correspondence from an Irvine resident
  regarding her positive experience with an Irvine Police Officer;
  reiterated the City’s “in partnership with the community” motto and its
  meaning.

  Received and filed.

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Agran noted prior requests to place certain items on upcoming
  agendas for City Council consideration, and subsequently renewed his requests to
  agendize these items, which included: 1) a follow-up request from the June 22, 2021,
  meeting with respect to the location and the forward movement of the Veterans
  Memorial Park and Cemetery in Irvine; and 2) transitioning to district elections in
  response to a letter received on behalf of Attorney Kevin Shenkman.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Agran to:

  Place the Veterans Memorial Park and Cemetery issue at the Amended and
  Restated Development Agreement (ARDA) site on the agenda at the one of the
  next two City Council meetings for discussion and possible City Council action to
  move forward.

  Motion failed due to lack of a second.

  At Mayor Khan’s request, William Marticorena, Legal Counsel, opined on the purpose
  of Council Announcements and whether a Councilmember’s ability to request that an
  item be placed on a future agenda was consistent with the Brown Act, following which
  Councilmember Agran noted his desire to also agendize the City Council policy that
  requires two signatures to place items onto the agenda.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  July 13, 2021

  Councilmember Kuo expressed appreciation to the Irvine Police Department and the
  Orange County Fire Authority for the joint outdoor Open House held at the Orange
  County Great Park on June 27; and announced three upcoming events at Mason Park
  in Irvine, which included: 1) the Fenians’ performance on July 15; 2) the showing of
  Toy Story 4 on July 23; and 3) the showing of Willow on July 30.

  Councilmember Carroll provided a brief update on the recent Orange County Power
  Authority meeting, at which time the Board considered the adoption of the Risk
  Management policy, received a presentation from Pacific Energy Advisors, Inc. (PEA),
  and approved a volunteer policy. He also provided a brief update on the recent
  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) meeting, at which time the
  Board discussed the Inclusive Economic Recovery Strategy.

  Vice Mayor Kim announced that she, along with Mayor Khan, had the opportunity to
  meet with United States Secretary of Labor Marty Walsh and Congresswoman Katie
  Porter, who toured Meadow Park Elementary School and the Rainbow Rising after-
  school program.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  The 2020 Irvine Global Village Festival has been recognized with a “Thumbs Up!”
  Award from CalFest, the California/Nevada Festival & Events Association. The
  award showcases events that exhibited resourcefulness in staging events in
  pandemic conditions. In 2020, Community Services staff created a mix of
  modified in-person events, online experiences, and at-home activities to bring
  the community together for the City’s Irvine Global Village Festival. This effort
  was recognized by CalFest with an award to “applaud new and seasoned events
  for their ability to pivot and entertain audiences during the COVID-19 pandemic.”
  The City is grateful for everyone who worked to make last year’s festival happen,
  giving the community something to look forward to and celebrate during an
  incredibly challenging year. This year, the community will be back together in
  person to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Irvine Global Village Festival with
  a full day of food, music, art, and fun at the Orange County Great Park on
  Saturday, October 9, from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. To inquire about sponsorship and
  vendor opportunities, and for more information about this year’s event, visit
  irvinefestival.org.

  •  The Sizzlin’ Summer Concert series returns to Mike Ward Community Park –
  Woodbridge and kicks off Friday, July 16, at 6 p.m., with the Irvine Barclay
  Theatre Jazz Band featuring the Ron Kobayashi Trio. On Saturday at 5:30 p.m.,
  Yachty by Nature will perform soft rock from the late ‘70s and early ‘80s. This
  free family-friendly concert series runs through August and covers a variety of
  musical tastes. There are three Friday concerts presented in partnership with the
  Irvine Barclay Theatre, five Saturday evening concerts, and a Sunday series
  finale featuring Pacific Symphony. In support of the City’s 50th anniversary
  celebration, the City is encouraging all guests to donate canned food and
  nonperishable items to help support families in need to reach a goal of filling 50
  barrels from the concert event season. All donations will support Families

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  July 13, 2021

  Forward. General Admission is free and lawn seating is available first-come, first-
  served for the entire community.

  •  Summer Fun at the Orange County Great Park is happening throughout the
  summer. Raya and the Last Dragon, the second film in the Movie on the Lawn
  series, will be shown on Saturday, July 17. The movie will begin after sunset at
  approximately 8:15 p.m. Open seating on the Terraced Lawn will be first-come,
  first-served, and admission is free. Movies on the Lawn continues various
  Saturday evenings through August 21. Community members can also stop by
  the Great Park Gallery to explore the process of animation from script to screen
  through original art, writing, and other works created by Chuck Jones, the artist
  who brought to life some favorite characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck. The
  exhibition runs through September 12. In addition, the community is invited to
  participate in ongoing art and creativity programs, educational lectures, and a
  film series inspired by Jones’ work and legacy. The third Irvine Summer Art
  Market will take place in the Palm Court Arts Complex on Sunday, July 18, from
  10 a.m. to 2 p.m. The market features unique locally made items and live art
  demonstrations. Admission and parking are free. To learn more about each of
  these family-friend events, visit ocgp.org.

  •  Many outstanding photos have been submitted as part of the 50th Anniversary
  Photo Contest, and the City looks forward to more submissions highlighting the
  people and places that make Irvine special. Community members can submit
  photos of Irvine in the following categories:

  o  Cultural and Community
  o  Historical
  o  Outdoors
  o  Pets, and
  o  Submissions from those 17 and under.

  The winners in each category will be revealed in the winter issue of Inside Irvine,
  and will be featured in an exhibition at the Irvine Civic Center. A grand prize will
  receive a $250 gift card to the Irvine Spectrum Center. Submissions will be
  accepted through August 31. For more information, including official contest rules
  and entry guidelines, visit cityofirvine.org/photocontest.

  •  The American Rescue Plan, signed into law on March 11, 2021, expanded the
  Child Tax Credit for 2021 to provide additional help to more families. While tax
  relief is typically available only when filing your taxes, Child Tax Credit payments
  will be provided monthly for the first time ever, beginning this month. This means
  much needed relief will reach families sooner and help each month with
  expenses. To help with the costs of raising children, families will begin to receive
  monthly payments of up to $250 for each child 6 to 17 years old and $300 for
  each child under age 6. Eligible recipients will receive this tax relief automatically
  if tax returns were filed in 2019 or 2020 and if registered to receive a stimulus
  check from the Internal Revenue Service. For more information about the Child
  Tax Credit, visit childtaxcredit.gov.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  July 13, 2021

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  2.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  ACTION: Moved by Vice Mayor Kim, seconded by Councilmember Kuo, and

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  6

  Cory Hilderbrand, Community Services Manager, responded to

  City Council discussion included: questioning whether approval of this

  3.4  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY MAYOR KHAN AND
  COUNCILMEMBER CARROLL TO CHANGE THE NAME OF THE
  ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK TO THE IRVINE GREAT PARK

  This item was agendized at the request of Mayor Khan and
  Councilmember Carroll, who requested City Council consideration to
  discuss changing the name of the Orange County Great Park to the
  Irvine Great Park.

  Joel Belding, Deputy Director of Great Park Planning and Development,
  provided a brief presentation and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about the name change
  process; expressed concern about the cost of renaming the Great Park
  and questioned whether a cost estimate to do so was available;
  expressed concern about rebranding; provided a history on the
  initiatives that were brought before voters to develop the Orange
  County Great Park (Great Park); questioned whether an agreement had
  been established with the County of Orange that required the City to
  use Orange County in the Great Park’s name; discussed additional
  alternative name changes; noted that the Great Park was a municipal
  city park maintained and administered by the City; noted that discussion
  of a name change was only in the early stage; suggested cost-saving
  ideas; questioned whether “Orange County” was displayed on current
  park signage; and suggested polling members of the public via a survey
  similar to the one conducted for the renaming of “Suicide Hill”.

  William Marticorena, Legal Counsel, noted that the City Council could
  take action to change the name at the meeting; however, staff would
  recommend that the City Council’s motion include direction to staff to
  return to the City Council with an implementation plan; and reiterated
  that the matter would also need to be submitted to the Orange County
  Great Park Board for consideration. He also noted that the agreement
  between the City and the County of Orange was not specific to the
  naming of the park and that there was no legal impediment to keep the
  current name.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  10
 City Council Minutes  July 13, 2021

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the renaming of the

  Susan Sayre, Irvine resident

  Todd Spitzer, Orange County District Attorney

  Kevin Corrigan, Irvine resident, noted his undecided position with

  Branda Lin, Irvine resident, expressed concern about the lack of a staff

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Khan, seconded by Councilmember

  Direct staff to initiate a feasibility study to include: 1) costs of

  materials, as are necessary to reflect a name change from
  Orange County Great Park, to Irvine Great Park or Great Park of
  Irvine; and schedule the matter for public discussion and vote at
  the July 27, 2021, Orange County Great Park Board meeting.
